fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed sits at 15, deep in extreme fear, about level with a week ago (16) and half its reading a month ago (30).

markets.summary: Wall Street clawed back most of a steep AI-led selloff on the last session before Thanksgiving: the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% to 7,182.78 after being down as much as 3.2%, the Nasdaq fell 0.62% to 23,585.80, and the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Nvidia fell 3.9% to $149.30 on hot PCE inflation and fresh tariff proposals, and S&P Global put its credit rating on CreditWatch Negative. Small caps held up better, with the Russell 2000 up 0.71% to 2,704.06, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.85%. Gold futures fell 0.7% to about $3,536 and silver futures 1.7% to about $40.05, both near multi-month lows and well below their 40-week averages. Breadth improved to 59.2% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, still neutral, while Fear & Greed remains in extreme fear. US markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.

weather.summary: A strengthening coastal storm will track up the East Coast through Thanksgiving, with major coastal flooding Thursday morning from the Virginia Tidewater and Chesapeake Bay to southern New Jersey, coastal gusts over 60 mph, and 1-4 inches of rain across the Mid-Atlantic. Snow is increasingly likely on the storm's western edge in the Mid-Mississippi Valley, while rain and mountain snow continue in the Pacific Northwest.
